key_insight: PC-GNO learns the full mid-plane six-component stress tensor field in concrete penetration by coupling graph message passing with physics-informed interface strength.
engineering_relevance: This enables surrogate field prediction for penetration-resistant concrete design, letting engineers derive multiple failure and energy metrics from one model instead of relying on scalar outputs or expensive mesoscale FEM runs.
method: Aggregate-resolved finite element simulations generate training fields for 359 impact cases.
Graph message passing is weighted by impedance contrast across material interfaces.
Spectral normalization constrains updates for stable operator learning in function space.
evidence_signal: The model is trained and evaluated on verified laboratory-backed data at 100, 135, and 165 m/s across concrete strengths of 14, 23, and 48 MPa, achieving 80.16% mean accuracy and outperforming the prior-frame baseline, Fourier neural operator, and linear regression.
watch_item: Performance is tied to the specific training/evaluation regimes and aggregate-resolution assumptions, so transfer to different concretes, projectile types, or geometries may require retraining or revalidation.
paper_title: A physics-coupled graph neural operator for mid-plane six-component stress tensor field prediction in concrete penetration
